title: The Great Awakenings
objective: After this level you can explain how revivals in the 1700s and 1800s reshaped American religion and grew the Baptists and Methodists.
summary: The Great Awakening (about 1720 to the 1740s) and the Second Great Awakening (about 1795 to 1835) called for a 'new birth', invented the camp meeting and grew the Baptists and Methodists.

cards.headline: Picture families camping for days in a Kentucky clearing to hear preaching.
cards.body: That was a camp meeting, the signature of America's revivals. Two great waves of revival reshaped the country's churches. Here's how.

cards.headline: The first wave
cards.body: The Great Awakening swept the British American colonies mainly between about 1720 and the 1740s. In 1739 and 1740 George Whitefield, an Anglican priest, preached up and down the colonies to vast crowds, while Jonathan Edwards became the revival's great thinker and defender. Preachers stressed God's unmerited grace and the "new birth" in Jesus Christ: faith as a turning point you feel.

cards.headline: The second wave
cards.body: A Second Great Awakening followed, from about 1795 to 1835. Its great invention was the camp meeting: families loaded their wagons, pitched tents and stayed for several days. In the summer of 1801 Barton Stone organized a powerful revival at Cane Ridge, near Lexington, Kentucky. The Kentucky revivals stirred intense emotion.

cards.headline: Who grew
cards.body: Revivals helped make the teachings of the Baptists and Methodists accessible to a wider cross section of people. In the second wave many churches grew, above all Methodist and Baptist ones. The revival also stirred reforms, including temperance and the emancipation of women.

cards.headline: The Great Awakenings: the takeaways
learned: The Great Awakening preached a felt "new birth"
The Second Great Awakening invented the camp meeting
Revivals grew the Baptists and Methodists most

questions.prompt: Which preacher toured the colonies in 1739 and 1740, drawing vast crowds?

options.label: Jonathan Edwards
options.rationale: Edwards was the revival's great thinker.

questions.explanation: George Whitefield, an Anglican priest, preached up and down the colonies in 1739 and 1740.

questions.prompt: How did the revivals help the Baptists and Methodists grow?

options.label: They made both churches official state religions in every colony
They made those churches' teachings reachable by more people
They passed laws requiring every settler to join a church
They moved worship into grand city cathedrals
options.rationale: Camp meetings met in the open.

questions.explanation: Revivals carried Baptist and Methodist teachings to a wider cross section of people, and those churches grew most.

questions.prompt: Revival preachers called for a heartfelt "new birth". Which of Smart's Level 3 dimensions did that stress most?

options.label: The material dimension
options.rationale: Camp meetings had few buildings; the stress was on the heart.

options.label: Ethics and law
options.rationale: The call was to be born again, not a set of rules.

questions.explanation: A felt 'new birth' is Smart's experience and emotion dimension; as he wrote, ritual without feeling is cold.
